appeals.passage_context: Exod.31.1-Exod.31.18 contains the artisan commission (31:1-11), a separately introduced Sabbath command (31:12-17), and the narrative tablet handoff (31:18) that closes the Sinai speech and launches the breach sequence.
appeals.rationale: Exodus 31:12 restarts divine speech with a new obligation, subject, sanction, and covenant-sign closure. Verse 18 changes from prescriptive discourse to narrated transfer and explicitly marks completion of speaking. These markers meet the same speech-act and functional criteria used for the approved Exodus 30 splits.
appeals.uncertainty: high: the whole span genuinely closes the instruction corpus, and verse 18 is only one verse, so parent-level cohesion must be preserved even if child output boundaries are approved.
appeals.why_boss_counterevidence_is_insufficient: Corpus-close cohesion establishes a parent relation, not necessarily a single retrieval boundary. The canonical Hebrew independently marks a new speech at 31:12 and a discourse-to-narrative handoff at 31:18; retaining only an internal map applies a different threshold from the accepted independent procedures in Exodus 30.
appeals.stop_rule_acknowledged: No third automatic rewrite; preserve for human or external-AI review only.

boss_ruling.appeal_effect: retain low-confidence parent and defer to human or external AI
